title: Accounting for Income Taxes
description: Understand current tax expense, deferred tax assets, deferred tax liabilities, and temporary differences.
html:
Accounting for Income Taxes

Financial accounting income and taxable income are often different because GAAP and tax law recognize certain items in different periods.

1. Current Tax Expense

Current income tax expense generally represents the amount of income taxes payable for the current year.

Taxable Income × Enacted Tax Rate = Current Tax Payable
Example

Taxable income is $400,000 and the enacted tax rate is 25%.

$400,000 × 25% = $100,000

Current income taxes payable are $100,000.

2. Temporary Differences

Temporary differences arise when the carrying amount of an asset or liability differs from its tax basis and the difference will reverse in a future period.

CPA Focus:

Ask what will happen to taxable income when the temporary difference reverses.

3. Deferred Tax Liability

A deferred tax liability generally arises when a temporary difference will produce taxable amounts in future periods.

Future Taxable Amount Deferred Tax Liability
Example — Depreciation

Assume equipment has a financial statement carrying amount of $150,000 but a tax basis of $110,000.

The taxable temporary difference is:

$150,000 − $110,000 = $40,000

If the enacted tax rate is 25%:

$40,000 × 25% = $10,000 DTL

4. Deferred Tax Asset

A deferred tax asset generally arises when a temporary difference will produce deductible amounts in future periods.

Future Deductible Amount Deferred Tax Asset
Example — Accrued Warranty Expense

A company records a $60,000 warranty expense for financial reporting purposes this year, but the amount will not be deductible for tax purposes until the warranty costs are actually paid in the future.

At a 25% tax rate:

$60,000 × 25% = $15,000 DTA

Valuation Allowance for Deferred Tax Assets

After recognizing a deferred tax asset, a company must evaluate whether some or all of that asset is expected to be realized.

If, based on the available evidence, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of a deferred tax asset will not be realized, a valuation allowance is recognized to reduce the deferred tax asset to the amount expected to be realized.

Example

A company has a gross deferred tax asset of $50,000. Based on the available positive and negative evidence, management concludes that $15,000 of the benefit is more likely than not not to be realized.

Gross DTA $50,000 − Valuation Allowance $15,000 = Net DTA $35,000

5. Permanent Differences

Permanent differences affect book income or taxable income but do not reverse in future periods.

Because they do not reverse, permanent differences do not create deferred tax assets or liabilities.

Temporary Difference Creates DTA or DTL
Permanent Difference No Deferred Tax

6. Income Tax Expense

Total income tax expense generally includes both the current tax component and the deferred tax component.

Income Tax Expense (or Benefit) = Current Tax Expense (or Benefit) + Deferred Tax Expense (or Benefit)

A net increase in deferred tax liabilities, or a net decrease in deferred tax assets, generally produces deferred tax expense.

A net increase in deferred tax assets, or a net decrease in deferred tax liabilities, generally produces a deferred tax benefit.

CPA Exam Memory Rule

Future Taxable → DTL Future Deductible → DTA Permanent Difference → No Deferred Tax

Key Takeaways

  • Current tax payable is based on taxable income under tax law.
  • Temporary differences reverse in future periods.
  • Future taxable amounts generally create deferred tax liabilities.
  • Future deductible amounts generally create deferred tax assets.
  • Permanent differences do not create deferred taxes.
  • Deferred taxes are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply when the differences reverse.

quiz.prompt: A company has an equipment carrying amount of $180,000 and a tax basis of $140,000. The $40,000 difference will result in future taxable amounts. If the enacted tax rate is 25%, what deferred tax amount should generally be recognized?

choices.text: $0 because the difference has not yet reversed

quiz.explanation: The $40,000 taxable temporary difference creates a deferred tax liability. $40,000 × 25% = $10,000.

objectives: Explain accounting for income taxes and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
